title: "Error Analysis"
description: "The systematic study of model failures to identify their causes and guide improvements."
term: "Error Analysis"
letter: "E"
category: "Model Evaluation"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Error analysis means looking closely at a model's mistakes to understand
what kinds of examples it handles poorly and why. It helps turn an
aggregate score into actionable next steps.

## Technical explanation

Error analysis examines false positives, false negatives, residuals,
subgroups, data quality, and failure conditions. It may combine
quantitative slices with human review of individual examples. Findings
should be checked against representative data rather than inferred from
hand-picked cases.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Two models with similar headline metrics can fail in very different
ways. Understanding error patterns helps prioritize data collection,
feature changes, threshold adjustments, model changes, or safeguards.

## How it works

Collect predictions and trustworthy labels on held-out examples. Categorize
errors by relevant factors, inspect representative cases, and estimate
how frequent and costly each failure type is. Use the results to form
testable improvement hypotheses.

## Practical example

For a penguin-versus-ostrich image classifier, review false predictions
and check whether errors correlate with distant animals, unusual poses,
backgrounds, or mislabeled images.

## Common misconceptions

- A few memorable failures do not establish that a failure mode is common.
- Improving one error category can worsen another or reduce overall
  performance.
- Error analysis does not replace a representative evaluation set.
